newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP says undecided on rate rise request.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP says undecided on rate rise request.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) has not yet decided whether to include a request to raise the nation's official discount rate as part of a proposal to rationalise government-affiliated financial institutions, an LDP official said on Tuesday.

"It is true that the committee is talking about requesting a rise in the official discount rate, but we are still in the process of wrapping it up and have not decided whether to include it in the proposals or not," the official said.
Asked when proposals will be drawn up by a group within the LDP which is discussing rationalisation of government-affiliated financial firms, the official said, "As soon as we can".
Japan's official discount rate has been at a record low of 0.5 percent since September 1995.

Media reports said that the LDP committee studying administrative reform will make the recommendation by the end of this month in light of last week's change in Japan's foreign exchange laws. They did not say what the extent of the rate rise recommended by the LDP would be.

On May 16, Japan's parliament formally approved changes to the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law in a bid to revitalise Tokyo's markets. It scrapped a rule limiting foreign exchange business to authorised banks, enabling freer cross-border capital transactions.
